newsitem.title: UK: Clean tankers mainly lifeless, Caribs perk up.
newsitem.headline: Clean tankers mainly lifeless, Caribs perk up.

text.p: The clean tanker market was torpid for the third straight week, with only the Caribbean sector showing any sign of life, brokers said on Friday.
The Caribs/upcoast market perked up by about 15 points from a week ago with 30,000 tonne clean vessels now achieving W185.
But other sectors were lifeless, and brokers E.A. Gibson compared the market with the washed out Wimbledon tennis championships.
"The few rallies were very shortlived, preventing freights from falling further rather than initiating any notable recovery," they said in their weekly tanker report.
Brokers attributed the low rates in the Middle East to a surfeit of tonnage and few saw much respite.

"Some owners have been willing to ballast to the Mediterranean in the hope of finding alternative cargoes, but these are also scarce with poor freight levels due to the availability of tonnage in that area," said Gibson.
Cross-Med naphtha fell to about about W200 for 27,500 tonnes and 28/29,000 tonne gas oil cargoes slumped to around W170.
But Gibson said, "By the latter part of the week, however, a realisation that things could only get better promoted a rally of enthusiasm and, hopefully, freights should stabilise."
Rates in northwest Europe were stable at best, with 22,000 tonnes fetching W200, while 33,000 tonne transatlantic cargoes dipped to W160. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4088
